2. The suit was originally filed by one Kalidas Mondal father of respondent No. 1 against the petitioners as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and several other defendants praying for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from entering into the disputed land measuring 14.54 acres described in the schedule to the plaint and/or disturbing him in his possession. Plaintiffs case briefly was that the land measuring 38.28 acres recorded in C. S. Khatian No. 4 of Mouza Shibpur Badurgachha belonged to one Ismail Sheikh under the landlords Manomohan Chose and others. Ismail Shekh had korfa tenancy in respect of 20. 02. acres appertaining to his raiyati right which came to be recorded in C. S. Khatian Nos. 5 and 6. The landlords auction-purchased the land of Khatian No. 4 in execution of a rent decree on 19 August 1936 and possessed the said land. Thereafter in 1941 Kalidas Mondal took settlement of the entire land of the jote from the landlord auction-purchasers by executing and registering a kabuliyat in their favor on 30 May 1941. Out of his lease-hold land Kalidas settled 23.74 acres with different persons, leaving 14.54 acres in his exclusive possession. In the year 1950 the landlords once again purchased the holding in auction in execution of a rent decree. The plaintiff subsequently had the sale set aside upon deposit of the decretal an-ear rents and continued to be in possession of the said land on regular payment of rents. But during the preparation of S. A. Khatian only 4.04 acres were recorded in his name while the rest of the lard was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No. 3 The plaintiff alleged that the defendants had been threatening him with dispossession. 

 8. In this case it appears that besides the oral evidence, voluminous documents were filed from side of the plaintiff which include, amongst others, C. S. Khatian. No. 4, C. S. Khatian No. 5 and 6, the sale certificate in rent execution case No. 754 of 1936, the registered barga kabuliyat dated 13 December 1938 executed by one Hanif Gazi in favour of the auction-purchasers, plaintiffs registered kabuliyat dated 2 June 1941 in acknowledgement of his lease of the land of C. S. Khatian No. 4 from the auction-purchasers, certain dakhilas showing payment of rent, the treasury challan showing deposit of Tk. 1340/- to have the auction sale of 1950 set aside the registered kabuliyat of the year 1943 executed by different persons in favour of the plaintiff and a series of barga kabuliyats by different persons in his favour. The trial court, relying upon the said evidence came to the findings that the superior landlords upon auction purchase in 1936 possessed the entire 38. 28 acres of land of Khatian No. 4 that they leased out the same to the plaintiff in the year 1941 and that the plaintiff, in his turn let out 23. 74 acres of land of his lease hold to different persons leaving to himself the remainder land measuring 14.54 acres. The learned Munsif also found that the plaintiff was in exclusive possession of the disputed land and neither the defendants nor their vendors had any right to or possession in any portion thereof by virtue of their alleged purchase. The trial court further discarded the evidence of the defendants with proper reasoning’s. In coming to such conclusion the trial court dis-cussed the evidence threadbare and also considered the attending circumstances.
